sections.h2: Where do Gilmer County property taxes get paid?
sections.html:
The Gilmer County Tax Commissioner collects the bill. The main office is at 1 Broad Street, Suite 105, Ellijay, GA 30540, reachable at (706) 635-4762, and it serves the public Monday through Friday from 8:30am to 5pm. Anyone processing a vehicle title is asked to arrive by 4:30pm. The office's tax website lets owners search a parcel and pay property tax online.

Georgia's Department of Revenue explains that county and county school taxes are collected by the tax commissioner. City taxes are different: a municipal government bills its own tax through the city clerk, unless the city and county agreed to send one combined bill. Owners inside Ellijay or East Ellijay should ask both the county office and city hall what they owe.

sections.h2: What does a seller need to know about Gilmer County?
sections.html:
Gilmer County lies in the Blue Ridge Mountains of north Georgia. The legislature organized it on December 3, 1832, and Ellijay became the county seat in 1834. Ellijay and East Ellijay are the two cities, Cherry Log is a census-designated place, and part of the Chattahoochee National Forest falls inside the borders. The county touches Fannin, Dawson, Pickens, Gordon and Murray counties. Wikipedia reports 431 square miles in total, most of it cropland or forest, and notes that poultry is the biggest piece of farm output. The Apple Festival fills Ellijay each October.

The Census Bureau counts 33,894 people for July 2025, which is 8.1 percent more than the 2020 base. Housing units total 19,380 and four of every five homes are lived in by their owners (80.7 percent). The 2020 to 2024 median value of an owner's home is $314,000, higher than the figure for the other two Georgia counties in the same QuickFacts comparison. Residents 65 and older make up 29.3 percent of the population, the commute averages 28.9 minutes, and 212 building permits were issued in 2025.

With nearly three in ten residents past 65 and a commute near half an hour, Gilmer is a county where buyers weigh distance and terrain. Expect questions about road access and the lot's slope in the Blue Ridge setting.

sections.h2: When are Gilmer County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Ask the tax commissioner for the due date printed on your bill, because Georgia lets each county choose. The state's default for ad valorem tax is December 20, and a local governing authority may move it to December 1 or November 15 or use installment billing. The taxpayer then has 60 days from the postmark of the bill before interest starts to accrue.

Georgia dates that apply to a Gilmer County owner
ItemRule
Property tax returnsFiled between January 1 and April 1
Homestead applicationAny time after the home becomes the primary residence, up to April 1 of the first year sought
Assessment appealPostmarked within 45 days of the notice mailing date
Payment window60 days from the postmark of the tax bill before interest accrues
Refund claimStarted within three years of payment
Mobile home permitApplied for within 30 days of placement, then each year January 1 to April 1

Source: Georgia Department of Revenue, County Property Tax Facts for Gilmer County.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Gilmer County assessment?
sections.html:
Wait for the annual notice of assessment and read the appeal instructions printed on it. The state says the notice must tell the owner how to appeal, and the appeal goes to the county board of tax assessors, postmarked no later than 45 days after the mailing date. The state sets that as the last day, so mark the calendar when the envelope arrives.

Call the Gilmer County assessors' office with questions about comparable sales, property record errors or what happens after a board decision. Gather these items before you call:

  • The parcel number from your bill or notice.
  • Photos or invoices that show damage, a failed septic system or other condition problems.
  • Recent sale prices of similar homes nearby.
  • The postmark date on the notice envelope, if you kept it.

sections.h2: What exemptions can lower a Gilmer County tax bill?
sections.html:
Georgia requires every county to offer certain homestead exemptions, and some counties add larger local ones. The application goes to the county tax office in some counties and to the assessors in others, so confirm with Gilmer's office where yours is filed. The state's rule is that failure to apply counts as a waiver, which is why a buyer who moves in during the year should file before April 1.

The same state page covers freeport exemptions on commercial and industrial inventory, which exist only where voters adopted them and are filed with the assessors. An owner of farmland or forest should ask the assessors whether a preferential assessment such as conservation use applies and which form to use.

sections.h2: What happens if Gilmer County taxes go unpaid before a sale?
sections.html:
The state's county facts page says unpaid taxes can collect interest after the 60 day window and may also accrue penalties. The tax commissioner is the person to ask about any balance, an execution or older years owed, at (706) 635-4762.

A seller who is behind should ask for a payoff figure before accepting an offer. Any open tax is paid at closing out of the proceeds, so a low offer on a house with several years owed may leave less cash than it appears. A mobile home is returned to the tax commissioner by April 1 each year, so a seller of one should ask whether the home and the land sit under separate accounts.

sections.h2: How does a house sale work in Gilmer County with tax due?
sections.html:
Tax due is a title issue, so the title company or attorney requests the balance from the Ellijay office and pays it through closing. Georgia records deeds with the clerk of superior court, and long-term notes secured by real estate carry an intangible recording tax of $1.50 for each $500 of the note's face amount, collected by the clerk in most counties and by the tax commissioner in a few. Ask the Gilmer clerk where the tax is collected.

We buy Gilmer County houses as-is for cash. That can suit an heir who lives out of state, a seller with a deferred roof or well problem, or an owner who wants a closing date that does not depend on a buyer's loan approval. If the house was left through a recorded beneficiary deed, our Georgia transfer on death page covers what the heir must record first.

faqs.q: Where is the Gilmer County Tax Commissioner?
faqs.a: The main office is at 1 Broad Street, Suite 105, in Ellijay, GA 30540. The phone is (706) 635-4762 and the hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30am to 5pm.

faqs.q: What is the state's default due date for Georgia property tax?
faqs.a: December 20. A county may change it to December 1 or November 15, so check the due date printed on your Gilmer County bill.

faqs.q: Do I have 45 days or 60 days?
faqs.a: Both numbers apply to different things. You have 45 days from the mailing date of the assessment notice to appeal value, and 60 days from the tax bill's postmark to pay before interest starts.

faqs.q: Is Gilmer County's median home value higher than nearby counties?
faqs.a: In the Census Bureau's comparison, Gilmer's 2020 to 2024 median of $314,000 is above Gordon County's $222,900 and Glynn County's $301,300.

faqs.q: Can I apply for homestead exemption after April 1?
faqs.a: The state allows an application through April 1 of the first year the exemption is sought, and failure to apply is a waiver. Ask the Gilmer office what it can accept after that date.
